findings.why: I don't know what FNAC means. It is word I never hear before.

findings.quote: A nodule is a lump in the gland.
findings.why: The word nodule I don't understand. Is it bad or not?
I don't know what trachea is. It is not word I know.

findings.quote: The skin is usually numbed first with an injection. This stings briefly.
findings.why: I am very scared of needles. The word stings make my heart beat fast.

findings.quote: Sometimes the sample is not clear enough to give an answer, and the test needs to be repeated.
findings.why: This make me worried. If need repeat, maybe it is bad cancer?
I will worry for two whole weeks before I know my body.

findings.quote: Sometimes the sample is not clear enough to give an answer, and the test needs to be repeated.
findings.why: I want to know what happens next if this happens - another appointment, extra cost, more waiting.
Then it says call after 3 weeks. Why the gap and who decides?

findings.quote: If you have not heard after 3 weeks, please call the department.
findings.why: I don't know if results come by phone, letter, or online.

findings.quote: Contact the department if you have bleeding, swelling or pain that is getting worse.
findings.why: I don't know how many hours or days after this is normal versus an emergency.
It doesn't say if I can drive myself home or need someone with me after the numbing injection.

findings.quote: You can go back to your usual activities straight away.
findings.why: It says straight away but doesn't mention heavy lifting, exercise, or working at a desk that day.
FNAC is an acronym that is never expanded, so I do not know what the letters stand for or what the full name of the procedure is.

findings.quote: Most lumps like this are not cancer,
findings.why: This reassurance gives no percentage or statistic, so I cannot judge how reassuring it actually is when I am worried about cancer.

findings.quote: Contact the department if you have bleeding, swelling or pain that is getting worse.
findings.why: No phone number, email, or after-hours contact is given anywhere, so I would not know how to actually reach them.

findings.quote: Sometimes the sample is not clear enough to give an answer, and the test needs to be repeated.
findings.why: 'Sometimes' gives no frequency, and repeating means waiting longer without knowing whether it is cancer or not.

findings.quote: The skin is usually numbed first with an injection.
findings.why: 'Usually' does not say how often it is used or what would happen if the skin were not numbed.

findings.quote: Contact the department if you have bleeding, swelling or pain that is getting worse.
findings.why: It does not say how much bleeding or how fast-swelling would be an emergency versus something to simply monitor.
